analysis: The code snippet calls substring in two places within the if block where line.contains("=") is true. The first call uses substring with two arguments: substring(0, line.indexOf("=")). The second call uses substring with one argument: substring(line.indexOf("=") + 1). The only exception documented by the API is IndexOutOfBoundsException. For the first call, beginIndex=0 is non-negative and endIndex is line.indexOf("=") which is non-negative and less than line.length() because the '=' character is present. Additionally, beginIndex <= endIndex since 0 <= any non-negative index. For the second call, beginIndex = line.indexOf("=") + 1, which is at least 1 and at most line.length() (when '=' is the last character, beginIndex equals line.length(), which is allowed). Therefore, both calls are safe from IndexOutOfBoundsException. Moreover, the code only enters the if block when the line is non-empty and contains '=', so these conditions are guaranteed.
remark: No exceptions are triggered because the code checks that the line contains '=' before calling substring, ensuring that the indices are valid. The first substring call uses a valid beginIndex (0) and endIndex (position of '='). The second substring call uses beginIndex = position of '=' + 1, which either points to a character or to the end of the string (allowed). Since the line is non-empty and contains '=', these indices are always within bounds.
